subject: Can xlim() and ylim() accept geometries like polygons as arguments?

messages.author: 4a248770402c04bc
messages.subject: Can xlim() and ylim() accept geometries like polygons as arguments?
parts:
I'm using ggplot2 for plotting spatial data. I want my plots to look something like this:

In order to have the colored layer (mean) appear as the multi-polygon that it does, I've had to take some undesirable measures. I've taken a data frame of mean values corresponding to lat and long coordinates, which is at a 1 degree resolution, converted it to a raster, up-sized the raster by 10^5x pixels, clipped the resulting monster-raster to the boundaries of a multi-polygon in a shapefile using gdal_translate (outside of R), imported the up-sampled and clipped raster back into R, and finally plotted it. All that, simply to mask the area of interest for the plot.

It has occurred to me that xlim() and ylim() drop data outside of the constraints provided by their arguments. If those constraints could represent a multi-polygon, then I could use the original data, saving me the hassle of all that file manipulation and more importantly, speeding up the plotting by reducing the size of the data by a rather large factor. So my question is, can xlim() and ylim() accept geometries as arguments and if so, then how?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Can xlim() and ylim() accept geometries like polygons as arguments?
parts:
Short answer: No. The arguments to xlim must be either numeric, factor or character. See ?ggplot2::xlim.

Dennis
